repository.label: Identify discs
repository.description: Finds the PlayStation 2 images in baserom/ and checks each one's size and SHA-1 against games/*/game.json.

repository.label: Verify every checksum
repository.description: The same, with every checksum game.json lists (CRC32, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256). Reads each 4 GB image several times: minutes, not seconds.

repository.label: Place inputs
repository.description: Puts what each game's build reads where it expects it: hard links to your images, boot executables read out of them, links to toolchains/. Never overwrites a file.

repository.label: Test OpenRAC's tools
repository.description: The unit tests of tools/ (no disc or toolchain needed).

repository.label: Update OpenRAC
repository.description: Brings the checkout up to date with the published OpenRAC.
repository.todo: Decide how players get updates: git pull in a checkout (refuse when the tree has local changes) or a bundled release of the tools. See docs/INTEGRATION.md, 'Open decisions'.

rac1/pal.label: Extract the assembly
rac1/pal.description: Splits the boot executable and the 19 level programs into assembly with splat.

rac1/pal.label: Build
rac1/pal.description: Compiles the decompiled C with SN ProDG and links the executable.

rac1/pal.label: Preview a level in Godot
rac1/pal.description: Opens the first extracted level in Godot's player, to walk around it. This is Godot showing the editor's scenes, not the game.

rac1/pal.label: Check the progress report
rac1/pal.description: Recomputes progress/report.json from the source and compares it with the committed one, as CI does. Needs neither disc nor toolchain.

rac1/pal.label: Extract the levels
rac1/pal.description: Turns the 19 levels on your disc into a Godot 4 project in assets/godot. About 20 seconds and 630 MB. Stops if the project already exists: it never overwrites your edits.
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. From a shell on macOS the same command extracted a level into a new folder and refused an existing one with a clear message. Then offer Open in Godot instead when assets/godot exists.

rac1/pal.label: Import into Godot
rac1/pal.description: Has Godot read the extracted meshes and textures once, without opening a window, so that the first time you open the editor is quick. About two minutes for all levels.
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. From a shell on macOS, Godot 4.7.2 imported one extracted level this way in five seconds; a 4.9 development build crashed on it.

rac1/pal.label: Open in Godot
rac1/pal.description: Opens the extracted levels in the Godot editor: move, add or delete objects and save. Your edits stay in assets/godot.
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. The project file is assets/godot/project.godot, as the action expects.

rac1/pal.label: Pack your edited levels
rac1/pal.description: Turns the levels you edited in Godot back into the game's level data, in a folder of their own; your disc image is never changed.
rac1/pal.todo: The packer does not exist yet (editor/README.md, 'Regenerate'). The scenes keep what it needs: each object's class, its place in the level's tables and its instance data. Start with moby instances (move, add, delete), write the packed level under build/, never into baserom/.

rac1/pal.label: Test the level editor
rac1/pal.description: The unit tests of editor/ (no disc needed).
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app. From a shell on macOS: 66 tests, OK.

rac1/pal.label: Build the game
rac1/pal.description: Compiles the decompiled game for this computer with the compilers it finds (on Windows, Visual Studio's C++ tools, Clang and Ninja). A few minutes the first time; later builds redo only what changed.
rac1/pal.todo: Run it from the desktop app on each platform. tools/build_port.py ran from a shell on Windows 11 (Visual Studio 2026, Clang 21): an incremental build, a rerun of hostgen, nothing to do. Another copy of the decompilation is chosen once, with tools/build_port.py --source DIR; the launcher has no setting for it yet.

rac1/pal.label: Play
rac1/pal.description: The game as a native PC program: its decompiled C built for this computer, drawn by OpenRAC's own renderer, with the assets from your disc.
rac1/pal.todo: Built by port-build. The port also needs decompiler_out (openrac-extractor --decompile) and the levels (editor/extract.py port) in <data>/port.

rac1/ntsc.label: Set up the toolchains
rac1/ntsc.description: Downloads and builds the project's patched EE-GCC and assembler (every download pinned by SHA-256), then extracts the level programs. Takes a while the first time.
rac1/ntsc.todo: Run once on Linux. On Windows it runs in WSL: decide how the launcher starts WSL (wsl.exe --cd ...).

rac1/ntsc.label: Set up the toolchains
rac1/ntsc.description: The same, in Docker on macOS.

rac1/ntsc.label: Build
rac1/ntsc.todo: Find the executable make elf writes (config/us/build/SCUS_971.99 per docs/building.md) and add it as the artifact; macOS runs make through host/run.sh.

rac1/ntsc.label: Verify the build
rac1/ntsc.description: Rebuilds and compares the whole executable's SHA-256 with retail (verify-baseline.sh).

rac1/ntsc.label: Extract the levels
rac1/ntsc.description: The level editor reads the PAL disc only, for now.
rac1/ntsc.todo: The editor's readers know PAL v2.00 offsets only (editor/README.md); NTSC-U needs its own table.

rac1/ntsc.label: Play
rac1/ntsc.description: The game as a native PC program: its decompiled C built for this computer, drawn by OpenRAC's own renderer, with the assets from your disc.
rac1/ntsc.todo: openrac-rac1-ntsc builds from this version's decompilation (port/, cmake --preset release); before it runs it needs the game's main in port/game/rac1-ntsc/hostgen.json and its library table (port/game/README.md). rac1/pal is furthest along.

rac2/ntsc.label: Check this machine
rac2/ntsc.description: rac2's own report of what this machine can do: Python, the toolchains, WSL, Wrench.
rac2/ntsc.todo: Run once; it may need requirements.txt installed first.

rac2/ntsc.label: Set up
rac2/ntsc.description: Unpacks your disc with Wrench into a runtime folder outside OpenRAC and prepares the reference build.
rac2/ntsc.todo: Needs two settings the launcher does not have yet: rac2's runtime folder (outside the tree; build/rac2-runtime works) and Wrench's wrenchbuild. Then: {python} scripts/setup.py --iso {disc} --runtime <runtime> --wrench <wrenchbuild>. Windows with WSL.

rac2/ntsc.label: Build
rac2/ntsc.description: Rebuilds the boot program and its 27 level overlays from the reconstructed assembly and the C.
rac2/ntsc.todo: scripts/build.py --manifest <runtime>/runs/<id>/manifest.json --toolchain <ProDG 2.0>: the run id comes from setup's output; decide how the launcher learns it.

rac2/ntsc.label: Run rac2's tests
rac2/ntsc.description: rac2's unit tests (no disc needed; rabbitizer 1.16.2 must be installed).
rac2/ntsc.todo: Fails without rabbitizer: say so, or install the requirements in a launcher-owned venv.

rac2/ntsc.label: Extract the levels
rac2/ntsc.description: The level editor reads the first game's PAL disc only, for now.
rac2/ntsc.todo: The editor's readers know Ratchet & Clank PAL v2.00 only. This game's level format is a close relative (docs/engine/README.md): give editor/ a table of its offsets and its section layout.

rac2/ntsc.label: Play
rac2/ntsc.description: The game as a native PC program: its decompiled C built for this computer, drawn by OpenRAC's own renderer, with the assets from your disc.
rac2/ntsc.todo: openrac-rac2-ntsc builds from this version's decompilation (port/, cmake --preset release); before it runs it needs the game's main in port/game/rac2-ntsc/hostgen.json and its library table (port/game/README.md). rac1/pal is furthest along.

rac3/ntsc.label: Set up
rac3/ntsc.description: Unpacks frontbin.elf, boot_elf.elf and i5bootn.elf from your disc with Wrench, then splits them into assembly.
rac3/ntsc.todo: Needs Wrench and wibo (downloaded into build/rac3/ by the README's steps) and a venv with tools/requirements.txt: a launcher 'Download helpers' action could fetch both, pinned. Then tools/setup_asm.py --target all.

rac3/ntsc.label: Build
rac3/ntsc.description: Builds the three programs and checks them byte for byte (prints MATCH).
rac3/ntsc.todo: tools/build.py --target all --toolchain {root}/toolchains/eegcc_2.95.3_sn_v1.36 --runner <wibo>, with the venv's Python; needs the wibo setting.

rac3/ntsc.label: Check before a pull request
rac3/ntsc.todo: tools/pr_check.py --target all with the venv's Python, once Set up works.

rac3/ntsc.label: Extract the levels
rac3/ntsc.description: The level editor reads the first game's PAL disc only, for now.
rac3/ntsc.todo: As rac2/ntsc's editor-extract: the format is a later relative; its levels are in the WAD the boot program loads.

rac3/ntsc.label: Play
rac3/ntsc.description: The game as a native PC program: its decompiled C built for this computer, drawn by OpenRAC's own renderer, with the assets from your disc.
rac3/ntsc.todo: openrac-rac3-ntsc builds from this version's decompilation (port/, cmake --preset release); before it runs it needs the game's main in port/game/rac3-ntsc/hostgen.json and its library table (port/game/README.md). rac1/pal is furthest along.

rac4/ntsc.label: Extract the assembly
rac4/ntsc.description: Unpacks the compressed boot image, splits it and its overlays, and writes the assembly with splat.
rac4/ntsc.todo: Run once; check whether it needs the project's venv first.

rac4/ntsc.description: Compiles the decompiled C with SN GCC 2.95.3.
rac4/ntsc.todo: Nothing is linked yet in rac4: the build writes objects to build/obj, so there is no executable to play.

rac4/ntsc.label: Audit the matches
rac4/ntsc.description: Compares every compiled function with retail.
rac4/ntsc.todo: Uses the project's own venv (venv/): add an action that creates it, or run with {python} once the requirements are known.
